advances: One integer coordinate and integer base centroid. The assertion is about a transported law and its moment.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: The base moment equation is $\sum_{i\ge1}i|K_{-i}|=\sum_{j\ge1}j|K_j|$, so the two torque marginals have the same finite mass and admit a coupling. If that mass is zero take the zero coupling. The segment between $(-i,x)$ and $(j,y)$ has its base-zero point at $(0,T)$, so convexity gives support in $K_0$. Integrating $w=1/i+1/j$ against the two labelled marginals gives the noncentral mass. The pointwise identity $wT=x/i+y/j$ gives the noncentral continuous first moment by the same marginal integration. Adding $\mu_0$ gives the asserted centroid and mass.

Let $K_z$ be its fiber and $\mu_z$ its $d$-volume.
